name.en: Fake bank “live chat” that takes over your laptop

how.en: A caller from your bank’s “fraud department” says a suspicious payment has been made from your account and they need remote access to your laptop or computer to block it. They send you to a website that looks like your bank’s and ask you to click “start live chat”. That downloads a remote-access app, which lets them control your computer and log in to your online banking. The “cancellation” actually sends your money to them.

text.en: A caller from your bank’s “fraud department” says there is a suspicious payment.
They need to act now to stop the payment.
They send you to a look-alike bank website with a “start live chat” button.
Clicking it installs an app that lets them control your computer.

Caller: To reverse that payment I’ll need to see your computer. Type the web address I give you, click the green “Start live chat” button, then accept the download that pops up so our agent can connect to your screen.

en: bank asked for remote access to my laptop
caller made me install an app to cancel a payment
fraud department took control of my computer
they could see my screen and logged into my banking
fake bank website with live chat
Anyone asking you to download an app or share your screen to stop a payment.
A website address read out on the phone that is close to, but not the same as, your bank’s.
Pressure to act before the payment goes through.
Hang up. Never install software or give remote access at a caller’s request.
Switch off the computer’s internet connection if they already connected, and ring your bank on the number on your card.
Report it to your local Garda station.

sources.title: Increase in phone scams asking for remote access to your laptop
